newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB details Prairie elevator space, railcar unload.
newsitem.headline: CWB details Prairie elevator space, railcar unload.

text.p: Vacant primary elevator space edged up in the past week across Canada's Prairies as railcar unloads at Pacific ports were nearly on target, the Canadian Wheat Board said.
Average vacancy in Prairie elevators was 18 percent in the week ended March 9, compared to 17 percent the week before.
Weather and equipment-related difficulties in shipping grains and oilseeds to Pacific ports from the Prairies since early January caused vessel backlogs on the coast.
Thirty four ships waited to load on Canada's Pacific ports with one ship berthed as long as 42 days.
Manitoba elevators had the least space available at 14 percent, Saskatchewan was next at 18 percent and Alberta had the most vacancy at 21 percent.
Vancouver saw 3,433 railcars unloaded in the past week, compared to the target of 3,400 hopper cars.
Prince Rupert unloads totalled 1,299 railcars compared to the target of 1,500 hopper cars.
Thunder Bay unloads reached 1,138 hopper cars compared to the target of 900 railcars.
